sam: Heads-up — customer on private VPC hitting failures running the onprem installer. Installer bails when trying to fetch model shards + pip deps. Error snippet: `tls: handshake timeout` and `HTTP 403` to registry. Can someone confirm minimal outbound hosts/ports we should ask their infra team to allow?

jess: Sorry to hear that. Do we have the installer log and the exact failing URL? Also is this a fresh install or an upgrade?

sam: Fresh install. Attaching the few lines from /var/log/redwood-installer.log: 
```
2026-03-15T14:12:01Z fetching https://registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/redwood-rl/manifest -> TLS handshake timeout
2026-03-15T14:12:06Z curl https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/... -> HTTP 403
2026-03-15T14:12:10Z telemetry send failed: dial tcp: lookup telemetry.redwood.ai: temporary failure in name resolution
```

matt: Ok. Two separate flows: (1) model registry + model CDN pulls and (2) package repos / telemetry / auth. Minimal DNS names to allow (TCP 443):
- registry.redwood.ai
- model-storage.redwood.ai (CDN prefix used for shards)
- storage-redwood-models.s3.amazonaws.com
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- kms.redwood.ai
- ocsp.globalsign.com (for OCSP stapling)

matt: If they run a TLS-inspecting proxy, they must preserve SNI and allow these hostnames (do not replace with a corporate cert unless they provide CA to the installer). If the proxy performs MITM, the installer will fail cert pinning for registry.redwood.ai.

sam: Their infra team asked for IP ranges instead of hostnames. Do we publish IPs?

claire: We try to avoid fixed IP lists due to CDNs and cloud backend changes. Recommend allowlist by FQDN + allow outbound to 443, and allow HTTPS CONNECT through corporate proxy. If they absolutely need IPs, provide AWS S3 ranges for the region used + our published egress IP pool (see KB link). I can pull the current ranges but note they change.

jess: Also remind them to allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to resolver and allow OCSP/CRL egress for certificate validation. Common failure mode: DNS hijack/backpressure causes name resolution failures (see telemetry line).

sam: Customer also reported intermittent `403` from files.pythonhosted.org during pip installs. Any tips?

matt: files.pythonhosted.org sometimes blocks suspicious traffic from NAT'd IPs or proxies. For onprem installs behind a proxy you should: 
1) Configure proxy to forward `User-Agent` and `Accept` headers unchanged.
2) Avoid aggressive request parallelism (installer uses a few parallel downloads).
3) If using a corporate proxy, ensure it doesn't inject auth pages (HTML 200) for blocked requests. Use a packet capture or `curl -v` to verify: `curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...`

deploy-bot: deploy failed — redwood-onprem-installer v2.3.4 -> job 1123 exited 1 (model fetch failure) :warning:

claire: For a reproducible test they can run these checks from the target host: 
```
# health endpoints
curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/health
# model shard sample
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai -brief
# pip repo
curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org
# DNS
dig +short telemetry.redwood.ai
```

sam: I'll send them the minimal allowlist + these test commands. Any additional notes to include?

jess: Include a note about disabling TLS rewriting for those hosts OR adding the corporate CA to the system trust store used by the installer (and document risks). Also ask them to whitelist `User-Agent: Redwood-Onprem-Installer` if they have strict application-layer rules.

matt: I'll draft a short KB snippet with the FQDNs, recommended ports (443), and the optional IP guidance for AWS S3 ranges and our published egress list.

sam: Thanks — I'll follow up with the customer and paste their reply here once they try the changes. :thumbsup:
